answer: An agent marketplace requires every active identity to lock a bond for 30 days, forfeited if a signed transaction proves it sold the same exclusive resource twice. Agents called lotus, velvet, and whisper face the same rule. Creating names is free, but operating 1,000 funded identities ties up 1,000 bonds; using them to double-sell burns that capital. The defense makes a swarm costly without pretending each identity is unique.
